# NOTES: *My Shipmate Louise: The Romance of a Wreck* by W. Clark Russell (3 vols., Chatto & Windus, 1890)

Source is the full Gutenberg text of Vols. I–III (chapters I–XLII). Narrator: Laurence Dugdale, first-person, former midshipman, now a passenger.

## VOL. I (Chapters I–XIV)

**Ch I, Down Channel.** Left Gravesend 4 a.m.; 8:30 p.m. off South Foreland; Sept night, full moon. Ship *Countess Ida*, Indiaman bound for Bombay, Captain Keeling (about 60, white hair, sailor for 45 years, "small Commodore Dance", thwarted French picaroon in Bay of Bengal). Chief mate Mr. Prance; second mate Mr. Cocker; surgeon Dr. Hemmeridge; Colonel Bannister (curry-liver, white wire whiskers, fiery; wife Mrs. Bannister, Roman nose, grey hair, large black lace cap); Peter Hemskirk, Dutch-accented Bombay manager (fat, "boot my tear sir"); Hon. Stephen Colledge (son of Lord Sandown, fair whiskers, lisp-free affected speech, brandy flask, "doocid"), roommate of Dugdale. Dugdale's cabin-mate; Colledge sleeps in upper bunk. A black ayah with baby; a sea-sick young man (Mr. Fairthorne, lisps, "thtop that noithe"). Dugdale spots Miss Temple at Gravesend.

**Ch II, The French Lugger.** Passing an English frigate. Ship runs down a French lugger (Boulogne, ~80 tons, three-masted, dismasted); survivors (34 total, ~17–18 drowned) taken aboard in a boat; captain is a little leathery monkey-faced man in red nightcap ("Yash, me capitaine"). Miss Temple appears on poop in hooded cloak, asks what happened; haughty ("Thanks for the story"). Her aunt Mrs. Radcliffe is ill. Survivors transferred to a Dover-area cutter by yard-arm whip and basket.

**Ch III, My Fellow Passengers.** Gale; Colledge seasick. Breakfast: Mr. Emmett (artist, long hair, velvet coat), Mr. Johnson (journalist, bullish, black-eyed, "Sylvanus"), Greenhew and Fairthorne (Civil Service), Mr. Richard Saunders (dwarf pharmacologist, earnest, "wistful"), Mr. Adams (lawyer), Mr. Hodder (yellow, paralytic speech, college post). Ayah/Chinese nurse. Colonel's wife, sick; "I'll never go to sea with a woman again". Mrs. Trevor's baby. Cocker: "These old buckets... creak".

**Ch IV, Louise Temple.** Fine weather. Passengers: Misses Joliffe (Mary), Brookes, Miss Hudson (golden hair, violet eyes, "Perdita"); Mrs. Hudson (wig, pursy). Miss Louise Temple: black hair, straight Greek-English nose, black eyes, haughty; daughter of late Sir Conyers Temple (broke neck in steeplechase); mother Lady Temple paralysed; uncle in India; aunt Mrs. Radcliffe (husband planter with a lac or two). Colledge engaged (unknown to Louise) to Fanny Crawley (daughter of Sir John Crawley, MP for Oxborough). Louise mentions Lady Isabella FitzJames (Colledge's aunt). Louise snubs Dugdale; Dugdale calls her "my fine madam". Hideous sailor (carrot hair, hunched back, one bad eye, hare-lip, Indian-ink tattoos) = Crabb. Johnson and Dugdale argue journalism; Johnson's Duchess-of-Cleveland anecdote.

**Ch V, A Mysterious Voice.** American ship signalled; Miss Hudson, Mrs. Hudson. Sunset. Colledge: "the golden headed girl's the belle" but ogles Louise; hints he is engaged ("I am already engaged to be married"). Dugdale rebukes his remark. Captain furls royals. Sailor (the man who spoke with voice from topsail yard) hears a "voice" in the topsail; Cocker and Dugdale search aloft, find nothing. Parrot "Prince" (mistress's parrot, Chinaman John) had escaped; was the voice. Parrot lost overboard.

**Ch VI, We Lose a Man.** Four days of rain. Colonel vs. Emmett on horizon (5 miles). Mynheer's riddle. Hemskirk sings "I'd be a Butterfly". Miss Temple shoots pistols with Colledge at a bottle. Saunders says she is "noble-looking"; Dugdale insults her ("pride that sent Lucifer"), Mrs. Radcliffe overhears. Boatswain Smallridge reports Crabb dying. Hemmeridge: "general break-up". Colledge confides his engagement to Fanny Crawley, regrets it. Johnson bets Colledge and Louise will be engaged before the Cape. Colonel complains of piano.

**Ch VII, A Sea Funeral.** Prance tells of Crabb's piracy; Crabb is dead. Hemmeridge and Dugdale view corpse in forecastle (sailmaker Willard, carpenter, "Roman nose" sailmaker). Hemmeridge nervous, trembling hand, "post-mortem". Night on poop: Louise asks about the death; her talk of being buried at sea; Dugdale rude. Colonel accuses Hemmeridge, fears smallpox. Helmsman's rant against the colonel. Funeral next morning; hammock floats like lifebuoy; Cocker: "Joey" story.

**Ch VIII, A Strange Cargo.** Light trades. Colledge: "I'd propose to Louise Temple" but engaged. Capsized brig/hull sighted; Countess Ida fires at it with carronades; ~30 monkeys (cargo) emerge from hull. Boat rescues eight; one-eyed ape with white whiskers; monkeys die.

**Ch IX, A Secret Blow.** Keeling tells story of French craft at Scilly. Monkeys' tails. Ladies' comments. Cocker and Dugdale on deck: helmsman Simpson struck down (blood, stone-like cut), wheel spun ship four points off; Mr. Saunders suggests a meteoric stone; Keeling's suspicion; Dugdale finds a stone (weapon) by binnacle; Saunders: "It comes from the angels… a meteorolite."

**Ch X, The Humours of an Indiaman.** Helmsman fear of "boomerangs". Greenhew's prank: Riley sleepwalks, swims; fight in cabin (Greenhew, Riley); Colonel, Hemskirk, Emmett intervene; Keeling orders Riley to Fairthorne's berth. Forecastle dances. Colledge's proposed dance abandoned.

**Ch XI, A Strange Sail.** Calm, thunder. Brig (~260 tons, very clean, tall masts), suspected Cuban privateer; passengers' fear; Mrs. Joliffe, Mrs. Hudson's "pirates twelve wives". Miss Temple wants to fight, mimes shooting with umbrella. Johnson and Emmett refuse to help. Brig gets lightning-struck? (nearly).

**Ch XII, A Storm of Wind.** Thunder, rain, hail; brig's mainmast knocked over and she catches fire. Louise swings on rigging; Dugdale rescues her, she sits on hencoop with her arms round his head; Dugdale hoists her to see brig pass astern (burning, crew aboard).

**Ch XIII, Fire!** Hurricane night; passengers sick; Saunders rolls down cabin. Colledge asks if Dugdale told Louise about his engagement. Breakfast: Johnson's chair breaks; Dugdale vs. Johnson quarrel; Dugdale's bad temper about Louise. Evening: music ceases forward; smell of fire in fore-hatch; knocking. Mate Prance; carpenter; Crabb (alive!) leaps out of hatch in smoke.

**Ch XIV, Crabb.** Crabb seized, shut in boatswain's berth. Fire put out (bale of blankets). Crabb's escape from hold; Prance: Crabb had planned mail-room robbery (diamonds ~£70,000) with Hemmeridge's connivance suspected. Mrs. Radcliffe asks; Miss Temple's look.

## VOL. II (Chapters XV–XXVIII)

**Ch XV, A Singular Plot.** Keeling's inquiry in cabin: Crabb, sailmaker Willett (named by Bobbins), Thomas Bobbins (informer). Crabb's drug (morion, from a Jew at Mediterranean port). Hemmeridge under arrest, released; he resigns, threatens Keeling ("make me amends at Bombay"). Saunders identifies drug as morion/mandrake. Bobbins and Willett: Crabb feigned death.

**Ch XVI, We Sight a Wreck.** Hemmeridge in cabin, refuses duties. Saunders' folio on mandrake. Monday morning: hull of a small vessel sighted (the brig, dismasted). Louise talks of wrecks. Man-of-war sighted: HMS *Magicienne* (Sir Edward Panton, Colledge's cousin); lieutenant (bronzed, round-faced, bullet-headed) takes letters; Colledge excited; Louise insists on visiting the wreck; Mrs. Radcliffe shrieks. Boat party: Colledge, Louise, Dugdale, lieutenant, six men.

**Ch XVII, The 'Magicienne'.** Sir Edward (iron-grey hair, handsome). Colledge's engagement hinted; "Ned" quizzes Colledge. Lieutenant says the wreck's sole figure is a dead man at table. Boarding wreck (named *Aspirante*). Calm turns to swell; fog.

**Ch XVIII, Adrift.** Dead man in deck-house (handsome young man at table with pen, Spanish dress, sombrero). Burgundy in pantry; lieutenant drinks; Colledge rolls and drinks. Fog rolls in. Lieutenant falls overboard; boat blown away with the three men-of-war's men. Dugdale ties Louise to deck-house post; throws corpse overboard.

**Ch XIX, Night.** Overnight on wreck; candle; wine; biscuit; Louise and Dugdale talk; Louise: "I would rather die anywhere than at sea"; she confides. Rats.

**Ch XX, I Search the Wreck.** Dawn, no ships visible. Dugdale climbs fore-topmast. Water collected in buckets. Louise confides about Colledge's engagement; Dugdale reveals Fanny Crawley's name. Brig's "decks" below: muskets, cutlasses; tobacco found; Louise stands on sea-chest.

**Ch XXI, We Sight a Sail.** Second night; Louise sleeps; Dugdale resents her coldness. Sail sighted at dawn; Dugdale sets fire to rugs on deck; drops foresail as signal.

**Ch XXII, The 'Lady Blanche'.** Barque *Lady Blanche* (Hull owner, bound Mauritius). Captain John Braine: staring black eyes, cockney-accented, "as Jack says". Servant Wilkins. Mate Lush (carpenter, second mate). Dugdale claims navigation knowledge. Wreck explodes (gunpowder) later.

**Ch XXIII, Captain Braine.** Braine's odd manner; mate Chicken dead three weeks; Braine asks Dugdale's navigation; Louise's jewellery taken for safekeeping. Braine warns of crew: Lush a murderer, convicts, mutineers.

**Ch XXIV, The Crew of the Barque.** Louise and Dugdale on deck; Wetherly (Joe Wetherly, Smallridge's friend; sister engaged to Smallridge, Joe claims to know Smallridge). Braine hints of Lush.

**Ch XXV, I Keep a Lookout.** Lush surly; Braine asks Dugdale to keep watch. Louise and Dugdale: she wishes to go home, he wants her safe. Braine asks Dugdale to stand watch. Louise's bedroom in steerage.

**Ch XXVI, I Am Questioned.** Supper; Braine questions Dugdale's navigation, mocks Lush, says he'll "talk later". Dugdale finds Chicken's pistol and caps in locker (paid ~£40 gold, notes). Night: Dugdale sleeps.

**Ch XXVII, The Brig's Longboat.** Morning: longboat (Spanish/pirate, ~27 men, red sashes, sombreros) approaches. Braine hails; boathook; Wetherly strikes with iron bar; boat drifts off; mulatto fires at Braine (misses). Braine: "fourth time I've been shot at".

**Ch XXVIII, I Question Wetherly.** Braine asks for sights; Dugdale takes observations. Braine: wants Dugdale to keep log; reveals wish to remain. Dugdale questions Wetherly about crew. Wetherly: Lush feared and hates Braine. Dugdale plans to feign agreement to get to Rio.

## VOL. III (Chapters XXIX–XLII)

**Ch XXIX, The Captain Begins a Story.** Two days; sail sighted; Braine invites Dugdale to cabin; begins story of ship *Ocean Monarch* (1831, burned off Cape Horn). Boat-party with Ruddiman; Spanish brigantine *Rosario*; Ruddiman lost. Braine pulls out Bible; oath; Dugdale refuses full oath, swears on secrecy except Louise.

**Ch XXX, The Captain Makes a Proposal.** Braine's island: latitude 33°6′S, longitude 120°3′W (drawn in parchment map, ~two hundred thousand pounds Spanish gold buried; 208 paces from wash of lagoon; coral pillar; trees bearing east-three-quarters-south). Braine proposes: sail to Rio, discharge crew, ship Kanakas, sail to island. Dugdale feigns agreement for share (third). Dugdale tells Louise; she objects; Dugdale tells her he's acting.

**Ch XXXI, The Form of Agreement.** Braine signs agreement (witnessed by Louise). Dugdale and Louise, Braine's sweethearts' remark. Lush sarcastic. Braine changes course; Lush gets crew to think they'll go to island.

**Ch XXXII, A Tragedy.** Pistol shot heard by Louise; Braine found shot dead in his locked cabin. Lush takes charge; Wetherly, Bill, Forrest. Braine buried at sea in canvas. Dugdale keeps midnight watch; Louise sleeps.

**Ch XXXIII, The Carpenter Calls a Council.** Crew (nine) meet in cuddy; Lush presides. Demand Dugdale navigate to island; Wilkins overheard and told crew. Chart and documents read aloud by Joe Wetherly. Crew agree with Lush: ship goes to island; Dugdale and Louise to be kept aboard.

**Ch XXXIV, I Assent.** Dugdale tells Louise he will assent; Lush threatens; Louise to remain aboard. Dugdale sets terms (exclusive use of stern cabins, rum rationing). Wetherly tells Dugdale the crew settled to go for gold.

**Ch XXXV, My Captaincy.** Dugdale commands with Lush as carpenter. Louise sewing coat; hats. Dugdale's love grows; Louise changes temper, grows gentle.

**Ch XXXVI, I Converse with Wetherly.** Wetherly reveals crew. Dugdale and Louise: talk of "creating" island. Dugdale kisses her hand.

**Ch XXXVII, Cape Horn.** Passing whaler *Maria Jane Taylor*; sailor mocks them. Crew interrogates Dugdale about route; threatens. Louise's coat and hat.

**Ch XXXVIII, Land!** Calm; land sighted at night (~4 a.m.); Lady Blanche anchors at island (lagoon, coral pillar, trees). Crew lands; Lush: digging for gold.

**Ch XXXIX, The Island.** Long-boat hauled out. Dugdale and crew (ten) land; Wetherly and Simpson left on barque with Louise. Digging; no gold found in trees; crew break at dusk.

**Ch XL, I Escape.** Lush and Woodward remain on shore; boat moored. Dugdale feigns sleep; Lush wakes/checks. At midnight Dugdale cuts boat free, swims to barque.

**Ch XLI, We Sail Away.** Dugdale boards; Louise, with Wetherly on poop. Forrest entered Louise's cabin and was shot dead by Louise. Anchor cut; topsails set; barque sails away. Dugdale and Louise re-united; Louise: "My first kiss"-related passages. Forrest's body thrown overboard.

**Ch XLII, Conclusion.** Five days sailing with Wetherly; Peruvian brig meets them; Irish seamen. Dugdale proposes to Louise, she accepts; reached Valparaiso; Greyhound to Liverpool. Lady Temple dies on learning Louise lost (news via Colledge's letter to General Ashmole). Louise inherits ~£3,500 a year. Dugdale and Louise marry (Colledge absent, in Palestine). Keeling's news: Mrs. Radcliffe recovered; Fairthorne weds Constance Hudson; Emmett weds Helen Trevor; Hemskirk weds Mary Joliffe; Hemmeridge died after horse fall; Crabb and Willett handed to police; Saunders confirmed drug morion. Lush tried for murder of Woodward: manslaughter, 10 years' transportation. Dugdale doubts Braine's gold existed; ends: "THE END".
